extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and educators interested in research ethics and scientific misconduct
extracted.subtask_description: A short case-summary of the Woo Suk Hwang misconduct episode describing unethical embryo-collection practices and fabricated research claims, with links to news and scholarly coverage. Intended as an example for studying research-ethics failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impermissible practices in collecting human embryos
rubrics_metrics.description: Woo Suk Hwang used impermissible practices of collecting the original embryos from the human donors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flags unethical/illegal human-subject practices in procurement of research material (e.g., improper consent, coercion, or other impermissible methods). The page presents this as a core violation that called Hwang's work into question; such practices undermine ethical legitimacy of the research and can prompt institutional and legal investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabrication of research results
rubrics_metrics.description: At least two pieces of his work were fabricated: the claim that he created 11 stem lines, and the claim that he cloned the world’s first human embryo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication (making up data or results) is presented as a central form of scientific fraud. The page uses Hwang's false claims as example violations; consequences cited across linked coverage include loss of reputation, retractions, convictions, and career destruction. Examples and news references are provided for verification and further study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career- and publication-level consequences of fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: A man who was once known as a ‘top scientist’ destroyed his career with instances of scientific fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that ethical violations and fabrication lead to severe professional consequences (public disgrace, retractions, convictions, institutional dismissal). This functions as an implicit evaluative criterion: conduct that precipitates such outcomes is a clear indicator of serious misconduct.
